newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's PDS says government to change "Euro-tax".
newsitem.headline: Italy's PDS says government to change "Euro-tax".

text.p: A parliamentary leader of the biggest party in Italy's centre-left coalition said on Wednesday the government would propose changes to its plan for a 1997 "Euro-tax" at 1900 GMT that should satisfy all its members.

"I think we are heading for a unitary solution," Cesare Salvi, the leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) in the Senate (upper house), told reporters after meeting Prime Minister Romano Prodi and other party leaders for talks.

Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's Italian Renewal party, a small centrist member of the government, said earlier it would unveil a planned alternative to the 12.5 trillion ($8.3 billion) tax at 1430 GMT. Dini said his version was intended to share out the "sacrifices" of the tax more equally.
Salvi said the government's proposal would be presented at 1900 GMT "and it will be the proposal of the (ruling) majority".
He expected Dini's party to back the government. "I believe the conditions are in place for convergence on the government text," he said.

Labour Minister Tiziano Treu, also a member of Dini's party, had earlier said the government would amend the controversial tax it aims to levy next year to help Italy make the grade as a founder member of a European single currency in 1999.

Treu said the changes would be intended to appease the centre-right Freedom Alliance, which has bitterly attacked the tax and the thrust of Prodi's 1997 budget. The package aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's projected deficit.
Salvi said the government's planned amendment would review the threshold for payments by the self-employed and would introduce measures to spur youth employment in the poor south.
But he reiterated earlier remarks by Treu that the total amount raised by the tax must remain unchanged. ($1=1,509)
